analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) Brazil Update, 2) Brazil Webcast Today, 3) Credit Views, 4) UK Budget Preview and 5) Week Ahead Previews
key_insights: Lula won the Brazil presidential runoff with 51.8% of the valid vote over Flavio Bolsonaro, defying the polls. His margin was more than 4 million votes.
CME November USDBRL future is near 5.56 (BRX6), a 10% move higher from last week, on about 1.75bn traded volume (~95k contracts of 100k BRL each).

FX circuit breakers on the local exchange trigger at 5.3098, +6% from Friday's settlement and below the CME-implied level. The exchange can revise this. In May 2017 the FX breaker was raised from 6% to 9% during a volatile session.

Trading view is that the BCB could intervene in FX today, likely through swap auctions of around 1bn to start. This would add liquidity and not defend a level, and GS would not read it as a signal to sell USD medium-term.

GS FX strategy (Teresa Alves) says the main channel from the result is a larger fiscal premium in BRL and other local assets. 5.40 is the level consistent with a 'more moderate' fiscal premium and 5.80 with a 'more significant' premium, similar to December 2024.

Flavio Bolsonaro has not accepted the result and says he will seek annulment. GS notes that in 2014 the losing party asked for an audit and not a recount or annulment, and that the 4 million vote margin makes it unlikely voting access issues explain the gap.

The government must present a budget by year-end adjusting for measures since the late-August submission. GS sees this as a chance for fiscal consolidation but likely still far away. Next year a Lula presidency with a right-leaning congress, where Flavio's party is the largest, may worsen governability unless fiscal issues are tackled directly.
Jason Brauth (Global Co-Head of FICC) describes credit as a bifurcated three-speed market: high-quality non-AI, AI, and lower-quality leveraged finance.

High-quality non-AI credit (most of the market, IG and high-quality HY) has started to soften, especially HY, but spreads are still historically tight. Brauth expects it to stay resilient until the macro environment changes meaningfully, with real money looking to buy dips and new issuance expected to underwhelm at higher rates.

AI credit trades wide relative to ratings given financing and hedging needs, and spreads recently made new wides. Brauth sees more differentiation between strong and weak balance sheets and is becoming a bit more constructive locally, with better valuations and improving issuance technicals toward year-end.

Lower-quality leveraged finance is the smallest part of the market but the most troubled in Brauth's view. CCC spreads are about 450bps wider on the year and the CCC to BB spread ratio is at an all-time high.

GS UK economics (Moberly) expects the Autumn Budget forecast changes to cut fiscal headroom from £24bn to about £15bn before new policies, as a stronger wage projection only partly offsets higher rates and weaker growth.

GS expects UK tax rises of around £5bn, well below 2024 and 2025, plus more cost-of-living measures, modest departmental spending changes to fund the Defence Investment Plan, and higher financial investments.
GS expects OBR public sector net borrowing projections to be revised up by about £12bn a year on average, leaving post-measures headroom around £16bn.

GS expects the FOMC to skip a hike at its October meeting (Wednesday) and deliver a second hike in December. The key question is how the statement changes the sentence about the September hike. GS expects little new from the press conference.
GS sees seemingly strong FOMC support for hiking every other meeting, implying a high bar to deviate from that plan through year-end, which should limit the impact of Fed communication.

GS expects the ECB to hold on Thursday with no change to policy language, and keeps its forecast of one more hike in December. A March hike is possible if energy prices keep rising, but GS sees a significant hurdle to faster hikes or a deposit rate above 3%.
GS expects the BOJ to hold at 1.25% on Friday. The October Outlook Report likely lowers the FY2026 core CPI forecast and raises FY2027 on higher crude.

Other week-ahead calls: RBNZ Wednesday GS 3.00% (last 2.75%), BOC Wednesday GS 2.5% vs consensus 2.25%, Australian monthly trimmed mean CPI Wednesday GS +0.29% m/m, and Israel national elections Tuesday with fragmented polling and an uncertain outcome.

risk_factors: A contested Brazil election could embed a larger fiscal premium in BRL and local assets.
Brazil governability may worsen next year with a Lula presidency and a right-leaning congress unless fiscal consolidation is addressed.
Spillover of weakness from AI and lower-quality credit into high-quality credit.
Lower-quality leveraged finance exposure to higher rates, an uneven economy and AI disruption.
Rising energy prices, especially gas in a cold winter, could push the ECB toward a March hike.
UK Budget outcomes: higher OBR borrowing projections and reduced fiscal headroom.
vol_and_positioning: Credit is split three ways. High-quality non-AI spreads are historically tight but softening, AI credit made new wides, and the CCC to BB spread ratio is at an all-time high.
Brauth notes it has been a popular trade to be long wider-spread opportunistic credit, and that trade has caused much pain in lower-quality leveraged finance.
Real money investors are looking to buy dips in high-quality non-AI credit, and AI credit is described as a popular client long in both IG and HY.
geopolitical: Brazil: Lula won the presidential runoff and Flavio Bolsonaro says he will seek annulment from the electoral court (TSE), citing irregularities in a 2-hour extension of voting.
Israel national elections on Tuesday with fragmented polling, many parties near the representation threshold and possible post-election switching of allegiance.
Energy prices are cited as an upside inflation risk for the ECB and the BOJ's FY2027 inflation outlook, including gas in a cold winter.

tension_points.bull_case: Brauth expects high-quality non-AI credit to stay stubbornly resilient, with strong corporate fundamentals, yield-based demand and real money buying dips.
tension_points.bear_case: The segment is locally vulnerable. HY has started to soften and spillover from AI and lower-quality credit weakness is the open question.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful change in the macro environment would end the resilience.
